headline: Nvidia Slides on Credit Warning as Markets Pause for Holiday, Then a Short Friday
body_html:
Nvidia was the story of Wednesday's session, falling 3.91% after S&P warned that its credit rating could be cut over what it called rising management and governance risk. Moody's took a calmer line, saying Huang's reinstatement eases uncertainty and leaving its ratings unchanged. A Financial Times report that the company has stopped shipping AI servers to four Southeast Asian countries added to the unease. The S&P 500 fell 0.29% and the Nasdaq fell 0.65%.

Chip peers followed. Lam Research fell 5.68%, Micron fell 4.57% and TSMC fell 1.96%, while the semiconductor group averaged a 0.60% decline. Beneath the surface the tape was healthier: 465 stocks rose and 194 fell. Energy led the sectors with an average gain of 2.12%, ahead of Materials at 1.85% and Consumer Staples at 1.27%. Apple rose 0.43%.

U.S. markets were closed Thursday for the holiday. Trading resumes Friday, November 27, with an early close at 1:00 p.m. ET. Next week, President Trump is due in Arizona for the TSMC factory expansion, and investors will watch whether the AI-related selloff steadies or deepens.

briefs.headline: Ambarella and Nutanix Suffer Steep Drops
briefs.body: Ambarella tumbled 19.77% and Nutanix fell 15.19%, the two sharpest declines in our universe on Wednesday. Urban Outfitters also dropped 10.33%. The moves stood out on a day when more than twice as many stocks rose as fell.

briefs.headline: Energy Leads as Oil Firms on Supply Fears
briefs.body: Energy was the best-performing sector on Wednesday, averaging a 2.12% gain. Crude rose on supply concerns after Iran claimed mine strikes on ships. Materials followed with a 1.85% average gain, giving the market a cyclical tilt despite the slide in technology's largest names.

briefs.headline: Memory Makers Slip Despite Tariff Exemption
briefs.body: Micron fell 4.57% and Sandisk fell 5.57%, even though Micron's products are reportedly exempt from new U.S. tariffs. Headlines also pointed to Nvidia testing a memory fix from Kioxia and an analyst urging large buybacks. Taiwan labor uncertainty remains a flagged risk for Micron.

briefs.headline: Proposed Brazil Tariffs Put Airlines in Focus
briefs.body: Washington has proposed surprise tariffs on Brazilian imports, including a 10% duty on aircraft. U.S. airlines could face higher costs from the proposed Embraer duty, and the measures would likely push up U.S. sugar prices. The proposals are worth following in the week ahead.

briefs.headline: Black Friday Arrives to Mixed Retail Signals
briefs.body: Some brands are opting out of Black Friday promotions. Floor Decor rose 7.07% on Wednesday, while Urban Outfitters fell 10.33%. Markets close at 1:00 p.m. ET on Friday, so the shopping day will be judged through a shortened session.

briefs.headline: TSMC Expansion Draws Presidential Attention
briefs.body: President Trump travels to Arizona next week for an expansion of TSMC's chip factories. Separately, the company has proposed an advanced wafer facility in Texas. TSMC shares fell 1.96% on Wednesday as the AI trade weakened.
